# LifeKeel

> A shared family list. LifeKeel keeps what a family would look for on one
> list: policies, cars, school dates and who to call. Every adult is asked to
> confirm they have seen it, and a change asks everyone to look again. It also
> gives first steps when something happens, and a few money questions on the
> family's own figures. Not a budgeting app, not an AI financial advisor.
> Informational and educational only; not financial, investment, tax, or legal
> advice, and not a substitute for professional emergency services.

LifeKeel is free to start, with no credit card required. It never moves money
or buys products. Anything it sends for a person, such as emails to people they
name if they go quiet, stays off until they switch it on.

## What a family can do

Everything below works from what the family adds. LifeKeel shows, estimates and
drafts. The family decides.

- Find it ("Where's the...?"): policies, cars and school dates on one list;
  papers that every adult can open; wills and papers on file; who to call, from
  the policy papers on file.
- Everyone knows ("Do you know about...?"): each adult confirms they have seen
  the list, and a change asks everyone to look again. Someone can be excused,
  for example if they are unwell. An adult joins with a code and the organizer
  approves. The organizer chooses who can change the list. Children are never
  asked to confirm.
- Dates, not surprises ("What's coming up?"): MOT, renewal and fees dates from
  the dates the family adds; a monthly note of what changed; policy renewals
  and duplicate policies for the same person.
- Money questions ("What if we...?"): how many months savings would last; a
  "what if" for a change in pay or costs; cover on file against a rough
  estimate; retirement and education pace; debt health.
- Where to start ("Something's happened."): first steps that fit what is on the
  list; steps for seven kinds of bad day, which start when the person says what
  happened; a claim packet and a draft message to the person's own insurer, for
  them to edit and send; optional emails to people they name if they go quiet.
- A list that keeps up ("Things have changed."): any adult can leave, and a
  person who is removed is cut off at once.

## Keel Plus (paid, 7.99 pounds a month, cancel any time)

- Reads provider, policy number, amount and dates from an uploaded policy, for
  the person to confirm.
- A plain-language summary of financial email.

## Trust and data handling

- Connector passwords and access tokens are encrypted before they are stored.
- Financial data is never sold. Approved AI providers process it only for the
  request; the privacy notice lists who they are.
- No commissions and no ads. Revenue is subscriptions only.
- People can export their data and delete their account themselves from
  Settings.
